tasks.short: Grade communications work and transfer checked results

steps.what: Read students' assignments and papers for argument, reporting quality and communication choices
Check assignments and papers against stated length and citation-format requirements
Evaluate students' work and decide grades against the communications rubric
Write feedback on students' assignments from the teacher's marking points

loop.purpose: Draft feedback from the teacher's completed marking decisions
loop.input: Teacher feedback points and quoted submission passages
loop.output: Feedback draft linked to each marking point
loop.check: Teacher verifies meaning, tone, quotations and consistency with the decided grade in s5
loop.stop: One draft; unsupported feedback is removed or written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning short marking notes into useful prose requires language generation

steps.what: Validate final grades, feedback and students' registry identifiers before release
Publish the checked grades and feedback to students in the course system
Transfer checked students' grades into the separate student registry

tasks.design: Use native {LMS} format checks and one bounded feedback draft from the teacher's own marking notes. After the teacher validates the complete result snapshot, publish the course result and transfer the checked grade to the separate student registry in {OTHER} through distinct gated actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mechanical checks, feedback prose and duplicate registry entry interrupt substantive marking.
tasks.enabler_now: Native checks, controlled feedback drafting and supported registry imports address different clerical operations.
tasks.still_hard: Evaluate reporting ethics, argument and originality without treating format flags as grade decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why a communication choice succeeds for its audience.

ambition.what: Give each marked reporting assignment passage-linked feedback on one audience choice.

reach.task: Reconcile released grades with registry receipts

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed format checks, feedback drafts from instructor notes and registry imports can support marking while the examiner retains all grade decisions.

assumptions: Boundary is one assignment marking batch through course release and a separate registry entry where double entry exists. Registry is the student information system in OTHER. Do not apply the seven-share import saving where grades already synchronise.

Students provide the submission; teacher provides rubric and format rules before marking. S1 captures the actual interpretive marking notes, and s3 provides feedback points. Registry staff already maintain student id, assessment id, attempt and roster; teacher confirms mapping in s5.

Test native LMS checks and export/import first. Format check failures and unsupported submission types are handled in retained s3/s5 time, with incremental repair allowance. Grade import uses only the approved ids, attempt, grade and assessment version; mismatches stop and use the funded manual recovery.

S5 checks the final feedback meaning as well as grade and identity. Its exact snapshot gates each action separately; any edit voids approval. S6's ordinary publish click keeps its small time; s7 saves only actual cross-system re-entry, never system runtime or a same-system save.
All shares are unmeasured focal labour estimates. No automated grading or extra free second marker is assumed. Local access and assessment rules must be checked before rollout.
unknowns: Whether registry double entry exists and native marking checks are already used.
research_questions: How often do source-file checks or registry mappings need manual recovery?

already_counted.description: Reading, grade decisions, draft corrections, final checks and release remain.

incremental.description: Maintain rules and registry mapping; recover failed checks and imports beyond ordinary review.

approvals.approved_version: final grade, feedback and student snapshot validated in s5; edits void it
same s5 result snapshot with registry assessment id and attempt; edits void it

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central cuts 8 format checks, 9.9 feedback writing and 7 re-entry give 24.9 gross and 23.9 net. Cautious case: unsupported registry interface retains re-entry, difficult files leave checks at 75% retained and complex feedback leaves s4 at 75%; 6.5 gross less upkeep 1 gives 5.5, above low 5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Choose course outcomes and current communications examples for syllabi, homework assignments and handouts
Prepare draft syllabi, homework assignments and handouts from the chosen course brief

loop.purpose: Draft assignment instructions and explanatory material from a teacher-authored brief
loop.input: Outcomes, timetable, template and selected sources
loop.output: Material draft with source links and unfilled gaps
loop.check: Teacher checks task validity, factual examples, source use and accessibility in s3
loop.stop: One draft; missing facts remain gaps and teacher rewrites unsupported instructions
loop.why_not_simpler: A template fills dates but cannot draft an appropriate communications exercise

steps.what: Edit the course materials for disciplinary accuracy, learning value and accessible instructions
Check the final syllabi, assignments and handouts with their release settings
Publish the checked course materials to the intended student group

tasks.design: Use the approved course template in {DOCS} first, adding a single bounded draft pass for assignment prose from the teacher's selected examples. The teacher edits the completed material and approves its exact audience and timing before publishing through {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly drafting instructions and adapting explanations consumes preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates and source-constrained drafting can produce a first version from an explicit teaching brief.
tasks.still_hard: Ensure exercises actually teach reporting, media ethics and audience awareness.
tasks.human_edge: Choose examples that challenge this particular cohort.

ambition.what: Offer an alternative reporting exercise for students needing a different practice format.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: course templates and constrained text drafts can reduce first-version writing while retaining source checking and pedagogical editing.

assumptions: Boundary is preparation through release of actual course materials, not lesson delivery. Source selection and brief creation are counted in s1.

Teacher supplies outcomes, chosen examples, timetable, intended level and exercise requirements. Course administration already supplies roster and release window. Missing sources stop drafting and are resolved within retained s2/s3 time.

Native templates are tested first. The loop removes first-prose construction and repeated instruction formatting only, retaining media-specific rewriting. Ordinary working saves are included at their tiny unchanged time, without gates or claimed saving.

The final material exists before s4; approval binds content, student group and release time for s5. Edits invalidate it. All shares are unmeasured focal labour estimates; upkeep is additional template and failed-draft recovery.
unknowns: Reusable template coverage and suitability of source examples for model processing.
research_questions: How much rewriting remains for ethically ambiguous reporting assignments?

already_counted.description: Brief, draft correction, source checks, teaching edits and release remain.

incremental.description: Maintain the template and recover failed draft passes beyond routine editing.

approvals.approved_version: final material, audience and timing snapshot from s4; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central first-draft cut 20.25 less upkeep 1 gives 19.25. Cautious case: current media examples require extensive rewriting so s2 retains 90%, giving 4.5 gross and 3.5 net. Brief creation, source checks and release remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead classroom discussions using selected prompts

steps.what: Find the selected case and source excerpts for classroom discussions
Write the prompts used to initiate and moderate classroom discussions
Save the classroom discussion prompts in the existing teaching notes
Initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussions with the students

tasks.design: Configure topic and source filters for the existing case collection in {LMS} and {DOCS}. The teacher writes and stores the actual prompts used in class, then leads the discussion without an automated moderator or a new progress log.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding an existing case and its source excerpt can require repeated folder navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case metadata and saved views can expose the chosen topic's sources.
tasks.still_hard: Balance participation, disagreement and the quality of evidence offered in class.
tasks.human_edge: Hear a misunderstanding and change the next question.

ambition.what: No increase in classroom load is assumed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native source filters can shorten case retrieval; responsive classroom facilitation remains interpersonal work.

assumptions: Boundary includes the discussion's actual short case lookup and prompt notes, followed by facilitation. It does not add attendance or post-class progress records.

Teacher already curates cases with topic, title, source reference and course unit; source choice and missing-reference repair remain in s1. S2 counts the real prompt writing, not new metadata capture charged as today's work.
Test native topic filters first. They remove case-folder navigation only; prompt authorship and live discussion remain. Ordinary same-system prompt save is tiny, retained and ungated.
All shares are unmeasured focal labour estimates. Student participation is unchanged outside labour; additional upkeep covers saved-view corrections only.
unknowns: Whether topic metadata already exists for the course case collection.
research_questions: Does a saved case view remove actual repeated navigation without new tagging effort?

already_counted.description: Case suitability checks, prompt writing, ordinary save and live discussion remain.

incremental.description: Correct saved source-view links when the case collection changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central retrieval cut 4 less upkeep 0.25 gives 3.75. Cautious case: only a few cases have useful topic metadata, leaving s1 at 90% retained; 0.8 gross less 0.25 gives 0.55. Prompt writing and discussion retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assemble and administer a checked mixed-format examination

steps.what: Choose examination coverage and questions for communications learning outcomes
Compile selected examination questions, instructions and marking keys
Check final examination coverage, wording, keys and release settings
Release the checked examinations to the intended student cohort
Administer examinations, handle access needs and respond to procedural questions
Grade closed examination questions using the examiner-approved marking keys
Grade open examination answers for media analysis and journalistic judgement
Validate final examination grades, marking exceptions and student registry mappings
Publish the checked examination grades to students
Transfer checked examination grades to the separate student registry

tasks.design: Configure item-bank assembly and exact closed-question marking in {LMS}, retaining coverage decisions, administration and open-answer grading. Validate the complete results before their separate publication and supported transfer to the student registry in {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Copying selected items, marking fixed answers and re-entering final results add clerical effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native item banks and marking keys handle exact operations; a supported registry import removes duplicate entry.
tasks.still_hard: Assess contextual media judgement and ensure the examination measures the intended learning.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise defensible answers beyond an anticipated example.

ambition.what: Review which closed items produce unexpected response patterns before reusing an examination.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: item banks and fixed answer keys can automate assembly and closed marking; open responses and examination validity require examiner judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is an illustrative mixed-format examination from coverage selection to registry entry. It includes actual administration and is not added to overlapping whole-course marking estimates. Shares are unmeasured focal labour estimates, not a universal exam mix.

Teacher selects items and approves keys and weightings in s1/s3. Students produce responses during s5; the examination system retains student id, assessment id and answer. Existing registry roster supplies assessment and attempt mapping checked in s8. No new response capture is charged to the teacher.

Test native item-bank, fixed marking and import settings first. Assembly retains revised instructions and layout checks. Unsupported answer formats and disputed key matches are manually marked in s7/s8, with extra failures funded in incremental work.

S3 approval binds the exact question, key, audience and timing snapshot for s4. S8 approval binds each final grade and student/attempt mapping for s9 and s10. Every edit invalidates its approval. Routine author saves and one-share publication actions earn no saving; registry saving is only actual separate-system re-entry.
No automated proctoring or semantic grading is proposed. Students' work and existing specialist support remain unchanged outside labour. Local assessment permissions must be confirmed.
unknowns: Closed-question share and support for native bank and registry import.
research_questions: Which answer formats can use exact keys without suppressing acceptable alternatives?

already_counted.description: Coverage, assembly exceptions, exam validation, administration, open marking and final release remain.

incremental.description: Maintain item-bank and registry mappings and recover failed marking/import batches.

approvals.approved_version: question, key, cohort and timing snapshot checked in s3; edits void it
final result and student snapshot checked in s8; edits void it
same s8 results with registry assessment and attempt mapping; edits void it

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central cuts 12 assembly, 10 closed marking and 1 registry entry give 23 gross and 22 net. Cautious case: incompatible item formats leave assembly at 80%, only four marking points are eligible and registry entry remains manual; gross 8 less upkeep 1 gives 7, above low 6. Open marking and administration remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher retains disciplinary and grade decisions while reducing repetitive preparation, checking and cross-system copying.
reach: Assessment coordinator: reconcile approved result imports.
role.ambitious_version: Provide more specific communications practice and feedback while preserving examiner control over assessment.
